description:
**How is AI impacting your mental health?**

**A conversation with Ted Patterson and Dr. Sheetal Ajmani**
Generative AI is quickly becoming part of how we work, create, learn, process emotions, and make decisions. For many people, these tools have opened up new possibilities. They can help us move faster, think more clearly, and access support in ways that were not possible before.
But as AI becomes more personal, more conversational, and more present in our daily lives, we also need to ask a deeper question:

**How is this technology impacting our mental health?**

The AI Collective believes in advancing humanity and technology in harmony. That means making space for honest conversations about both the promise and the pressure of living with AI.

Join Ted Patterson and Dr. Sheetal Ajmani for a thoughtful conversation on the mental health implications of AI. Together, we’ll explore emerging research, real-world case studies, and personal reflections on how AI use can affect stress, isolation, emotional dependence, reality-testing, creativity, productivity, and overall well-being.

This is not a fear-based conversation. It is a human one.
Whether you use AI every day, are just beginning to experiment with it, or are concerned about where the technology is heading, this session will help you pause, reflect, and build a healthier relationship with the tools shaping our future.

**What You’ll Walk Away With**

You’ll have the opportunity to:

* Learn about emerging research and case studies on AI and mental health
* Reflect on how GenAI use may be affecting your own well-being
* Explore the difference between helpful AI use and unhealthy dependence
* Discuss practical strategies for using AI while protecting your mental and emotional health
* Connect with others who are navigating similar questions in work, life, and community

**Agenda**

**4:30 PM – 5:00 PM**

**About Dr. Sheetal Ajmani**

Dr. Sheetal Ajmani is a physician turned keynote speaker, executive coach, consultant, and founder of Radiant Living Institute.

A highly sought-after professional speaker, Dr. Ajmani empowers audiences with practical, evidence-based strategies to cultivate stress resilience, lead with confidence, and create sustainable success. With over a hundred speaking engagements completed to date, her approach resonates with organizations across industries, including healthcare, law, insurance, executive groups, and professional women’s associations.

Dr. Ajmani is the host of the Essential Self-Care podcast, which has reached listeners around the world, and is the co-author of the Amazon bestselling book *Doctoring, Better*. She is currently completing her first full-length book, *Live Radiantly: Let Go of Others’ Expectations and Start Living for You*.

title: Monorepos, Frontends, and .NET
description:
**Monorepos, Frontends, and .NET**
Join us Tuesday, July 14th, as we dig into monorepos — how big companies like Google, Microsoft, and Netflix manage massive codebases, and how you can pull the same tricks into your own .NET + frontend projects!

**Schedule**

* 5:45 PM — Doors open
* 6:00 PM — Food, drinks, and networking
* 6:30 PM — Presentation begins

**About This Session**
Web Applications continue to grow in complexity. With this complexity comes many build pipelines. Many big companies like Google, Microsoft, and Netflix will setup monolithic repositories to share code between different components. We will focus largely on client side components using JavaScript or TypeScript. This talk will talk primarily about Lerna and NX from Nrwl. We will also talk about different package managers and using Workspaces features provided by them. Then we will wrap up by talking about how to include a .NET Application in a Monorepo.

**Speaker**
J.R. Kincaid has been developing in the Microsoft ecosystem since .NET Framework 2.0. He primarily programs in C# and is an accomplished Full Stack Developer. His current focus is closer to the front end of ASP.NET Core Web Applications using React.

description:
Register now! [https://events.zoom.us/ev/AjoIaqpz0A42xubLnsURs-BbvwwEkOFvg86kCqSCudrTW0lHN2-J~AlP4Qq7pTYq5CI7twrjIGbDU0uF30exUSUnCFFmZ3B1CgIqHT8ZdFT1PyL0Ka4B_IXAE9McsSSpE3BHHpIq0CeeRag](https://events.zoom.us/ev/AjoIaqpz0A42xubLnsURs-BbvwwEkOFvg86kCqSCudrTW0lHN2-J~AlP4Qq7pTYq5CI7twrjIGbDU0uF30exUSUnCFFmZ3B1CgIqHT8ZdFT1PyL0Ka4B_IXAE9McsSSpE3BHHpIq0CeeRag)

What does a roller coaster have in common with a refinery? More than you'd think. This talk applies bowtie analysis — a proven process safety methodology — to theme park ride control systems, showing how OT cybersecurity and functional safety can be quantified together in a single framework.

Theme park ride control systems occupy a rare and underappreciated position in the OT cybersecurity landscape: they are life-safety-critical and continuously networked. While the integrated system is unique to each installation, the components themselves are an integration of commercial IT and OT products, often managed by teams whose primary expertise is mechanical and electrical engineering, not cybersecurity. As cyber threats targeting industrial control systems grow more sophisticated, the theme park industry needs analytical frameworks that speak both languages: the language of functional safety and the language of cyber risk. Bowtie analysis does exactly that.

John will examine managing the risks in these ubiquitous systems using bowtie analysis, which is a visual risk methodology with deep roots in the process safety world, refineries, chemical plants, offshore platforms, where it has been used for decades to map threat and cause pathways to a top event, and consequence pathways from the top event to harm.

This talk is for everyone dealing with ICS/OT cybersecurity risks and their management.

title: Jonathan Stewart: Translytical Task Flows: So Much More Than Write-Back
description:
**IN PERSON MEETING!!!!!**
When was the last time a dashboard made you reach for your phone to film it? By the end of this 45-minute session, you will want to.
With Microsoft introducing Translytical Task Flows, Power BI now has a native Fabric-backed pattern for write-back. Update that row. Approve that line item. Override that forecast. These are all things we have wanted, and they are wonderful. If you are not using Translytical Task Flows for that, start Monday.
But there is more.
So much more.
That button connects to Fabric User Data Functions, and it is not just a write-back widget. It is serverless Python running directly in Fabric. You can pass report context and user input into governed business logic, access Fabric data sources through managed connections, inspect the verified caller’s identity metadata, call external APIs when appropriate, and do it without standing up a separate API server.
Write-back is just the beginning.
What happens when the button is not constrained to a table update?
What happens when it can reach past your warehouse, past your tenant, and into the systems and services your business actually runs on, while still answering the question of who clicked it?
That is what this session is about.
What you'll see, no spoilers:
One button in Power BI. Nothing pre-recorded. Nothing pre-canned. All live, in front of you.
We will end with a report doing something a report has no business doing.
Come see what happens.
Who it's for:
This session is for Power BI developers, Fabric data engineers, and BI architects who already use write-back, as well as those intrigued by the boundless possibilities of what Power BI can really do.
What you'll leave with — four reusable patterns and a sharper mental model:
\- See the data\-function button as an action surface\, not a form\.
\- Reason about who clicked versus who actually runs the work\.
\- Gate an action on server\-verified state\, not on a hidden column\.
\- Know when a report should reach beyond Fabric\, and how to keep that safe\.
Write-back was the doorway.
Come see what is on the other side!

title: 🧜‍♀️ AICHR | Connections & (grocery) carts
description:
Meet people and pick up your weekly groceries.

🤝 **A casual networking hangout in the grocery store cafe**
Chats, connections, & grocery carts is a relaxed, social-first networking event for curious, friendly people across Hampton Roads who enjoy good conversation and knocking out life errands at the same time.

This is not a lecture.
This is not a pitch night.
And you definitely do not need to “prepare” anything.

It is simply a low-pressure space to meet new people, have real conversations, and casually connect while wandering the aisles and picking up your weekly groceries.

Whether you are deeply into AI and automation, adjacent to tech and creativity, or just someone who enjoys thoughtful conversations with interesting humans, you belong here.

✨ **What to expect**
\- Casual\, open networking with a mix of builders\, creatives\, technologists\, founders\, students\, and professionals
\- Easy\, organic conversations while shopping at your own pace
\- Light\, optional conversation prompts to help break the ice if you want them
\- No presentations\, no panels\, no pressure to “network correctly”
\- A friendly\, welcoming environment for all backgrounds and experience levels
\- Come as you are\. Grab a cart or a basket\. Pick up dinner for the week\. \- \- Meet a few new people along the way\.

👥 **Who should attend**
Chats, Connections, & Grocery Carts is for:

People who enjoy meeting others without forced networking vibes
Builders, creatives, technologists, and curious minds
AI, automation, no-code, and tech-adjacent folks
Students and career switchers exploring what is next
Founders, consultants, operators, and professionals
Anyone who likes good conversation and low-stakes socializing

If you enjoy thoughtful chats and meeting people in unexpected places, you will fit right in.

🏪 **Why a grocery store**
You were probably going to the store anyway.

Hosting this event in a grocery store keeps things human, practical, and approachable. It removes the pressure of traditional networking and turns it into something simple, efficient, and a little fun.

Two errands. One cart.

💡 **Why this event exists**
Community grows best in relaxed, everyday spaces.

Chats, Connections, & Grocery Carts exists to create an easy, human-centered way for people to connect without titles, talks, or expectations. It is about building relationships, sharing ideas naturally, and strengthening the local community one conversation at a time.

Come say hi. Leave with groceries. Make a few new connections along the way.

title: Cybersecurity - Chesapeake Weekend Afternoon Networking (WAN)
description:
## **Attention Information Security and Cybersecurity Professionals!**

Are you looking to meet new people who share your interests? Whether you're considering a career in cybersecurity, just getting started, or are a seasoned professional, we welcome everyone for an evening of networking, learning, and great conversation.

### **Why Attend?**

Join us at **Woody's Raw Bar & Grill** in Chesapeake for a relaxed evening of networking with fellow IT and cybersecurity professionals. Known for its friendly atmosphere, fresh seafood, and excellent food and drink specials, Woody's is the perfect place to connect with like-minded individuals, exchange ideas, and build lasting professional relationships. Whether you enjoy a cold beer or prefer something non-alcoholic, you'll find a welcoming community eager to share experiences and knowledge.

### **About ISSA-HR**

The Information Systems Security Association of Hampton Roads (ISSA-HR) hosts networking and educational events throughout the region, bringing together cybersecurity professionals, students, and enthusiasts to share ideas, learn from one another, and grow the local cybersecurity community. Our mission is to promote the cybersecurity profession while supporting and mentoring the next generation of security professionals.

### **RSVP now and bring a friend!**

We look forward to seeing you there!

4140 Portsmouth Blvd, Chesapeake, VA 23321
